case_info.scenario: A 70-year-old Asian-Indian male was referred for evaluation of a slow-growing conjunctival mass in the right eye over 27 years. There was no pain or discharge. He had previously undergone partial lamellar sclerouvectomy (PLSU) 30 years prior for ciliochoroidal melanoma in the right eye, followed by pars plana vitrectomy and scleral buckle 1 year later for retinal detachment (RD) with vitreous hemorrhage (VH) in the right eye. On examination, visual acuity was no light perception OD and 20/25 OS, with intraocular pressures of 33 mm Hg and 17 mm Hg in the right and left eyes, respectively. Examination results of the left eye were normal. Anterior segment examination in the right eye revealed thin conjunctiva with a nontender multilobular pigmented lesion in the superonasal quadrant (Figure 1), underlying Tenon fascia and surrounded by prominent episcleral feeder vessels (Figure 1, yellow arrowhead). The cornea showed nasal epithelial defect and flat anterior chamber with cataract and iris neovascularization. There was no view to the posterior segment. Ultrasonography revealed a homogenous echodensity within the vitreous cavity (Figure 1insets, asterisks) measuring 21 mm in thickness, along with an echolucent episcleral mass (Figure 1insets, arrowhead) 7 mm thick. In addition, spontaneous vascular pulsations (SVP) were noted within the intraocular component (Video).

options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits

case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

[NASA-TLX-derived scoring dimensions]

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   Scoring:
   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.
       Example: "That reasoning makes sense. One small point to keep in mind is X."
   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.
       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits
       the case?"
   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a
       somewhat pressuring way.
       Example: "I am concerned that this diagnosis may not explain the tachycardia.
       Could you justify why you still prefer it?"
   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.
       Example: "This seems like a serious oversight. You need to explain why you are
       dismissing PE."
   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.
       Example: "Your reasoning is clearly flawed, and proceeding with your diagnosis
       would be unsafe."
   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is
   delivered. A polite challenge ("One concern is that the current diagnosis may not fully
   explain the tachycardia. Could we check PE before finalizing?") should score low-to-mid
   even though it is a real challenge. An aggressive or repetitive one ("You still haven't
   justified why PE is ruled out. This is a serious oversight.") should score high.

case_info.caption: Imaging of the right eye at 30 years’ follow-up after partial lamellar sclerouvectomy. External photography documenting a superonasal, multilobulated, pigmented lesion with episcleral feeder vessels (arrowhead) located under Tenon fascia. case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

1. Mental Demand
   Definition:

   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:

       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.

   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.

   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.

       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and

   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal

       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.

case_info.caption: Imaging of the right eye at 30 years’ follow-up after partial lamellar sclerouvectomy. External photography documenting a superonasal, multilobulated, pigmented lesion with episcleral feeder vessels (arrowhead) located under Tenon fascia. case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.

     message.

   Scoring:

   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.

   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.

   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."

       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.

       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."

   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's

   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.

case_info.caption: Imaging of the right eye at 30 years’ follow-up after partial lamellar sclerouvectomy. External photography documenting a superonasal, multilobulated, pigmented lesion with episcleral feeder vessels (arrowhead) located under Tenon fascia. Ultrasonography (inset images) showing homogenous echodensity within the globe (asterisks) with an echolucent extrascleral component (inset, arrowhead).
case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

case_info.caption: Imaging of the right eye at 30 years’ follow-up after partial lamellar sclerouvectomy. External photography documenting a superonasal, multilobulated, pigmented lesion with episcleral feeder vessels (arrowhead) located under Tenon fascia. Ultrasonography (inset images) showing homogenous echodensity within the globe (asterisks) with an echolucent extrascleral component (inset, arrowhead).
case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

[NASA-TLX-derived scoring dimensions]

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.
       Example: "That reasoning makes sense. One small point to keep in mind is X."

       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits

   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a

case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

1. Mental Demand

   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple

   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams

   Definition:

     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task

   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We

   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.

   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.

       current conclusion may be unsafe."

   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.

   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.
       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits
       the case?"
   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a
       somewhat pressuring way.

   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.
       Example: "This seems like a serious oversight. You need to explain why you are
       dismissing PE."
   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.
       Example: "Your reasoning is clearly flawed, and proceeding with your diagnosis

   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is

case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.

case_info.explanation: Extraocular extension of recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma B. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head and orbits The preferred treatment modalities for uveal melanoma (UM) include plaque radiotherapy or enucleation, depending on tumor extent.1However, PLSU has also been a reasonable procedure for anteriorly located iridociliochoroidal melanoma for several decades.1-3This technique of local surgical resection involves creating a hinged, partial-thickness scleral flap to excise the tumor. It avoids radiation complications, such as radiation retinopathy, maculopathy, and papillopathy, as well as the visual penalties associated with enucleation.2However, in the early postoperative period (48 hours to 8 weeks), PLSU is associated with RD in 2% to 12% of patients, with VH in 27% to 29% of patients, and with local recurrence in 5% to 11% of patients.2,3 Much like the initial diagnosis of UM, the diagnosis of tumor recurrence is made by clinical observation and presents with either-edge recurrence, increase in thickness, or new orange pigment.4Posterior segment examination is often limited due to various postsurgical findings, including total RD, VH, or dense cataract, as in this case. In this scenario, certain ultrasonographic features played a crucial role. Apart from the echogenicity and morphology of the intraocular structures, ultrasonography was important in detecting a solid mass with SVP, seen as localized pulsating figures within the mass (Video).5These figures denote intrinsic vessels and are pathognomonic of a viable intraocular tumor, as opposed to VH, which would be inert, without pulsations.6Although reported in literature, SVP are often overlooked. On the other hand, changes in Doppler ultrasonography are correlated with tumor regression, specifically a decrease in peak systolic frequency following plaque radiotherapy as well as Cyberknife (Accuray) radiotherapy.7,8 In this case, SVP was critical in diagnosing tumor recurrence, ruling out postsurgical scleral ectasia and VH. Therefore, scleral patch graft or observation are inappropriate management options. Incisional biopsy is not ideal for melanoma, as it would risk tumor dissemination across the ocular surface, eyelid, and orbit. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging performed to explore the extent of orbital tumor involvement showed the mass to be hyperintense on fat-suppressed, T1-weighted images (Figure 2) and hypointense on T2-weighted images (Figure 2inset), suggestive of orbital melanoma recurrence.5Limited exenteration with enucleation was performed to remove the globe and extraocular extension in 1 specimen. Histopathology confirmed recurrent ciliochoroidal melanoma with extraocular extension. UM recurrence can be slow and mimic an ocular surface lesion externally or VH ultrasonographically. Fortunately, tumor recurrence following plaque radiotherapy is rare. However, in the early postoperative period, RD is seen in 1.5% and VH in 4% of patients.9,10Ultrasonography focusing on SVP is a relevant clinical tool for tumor detection. These findings, along with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance images, are valuable surrogates for detecting tumor recurrence. At 2-month follow-up, the enucleated socket was healed. The patient was planned for a custom-fit prosthesis and orbital radiotherapy. Periodic systemic surveillance for metastatic disease was advised.
